current_route.title: 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic refinement with narrowed perturbation bounds
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually tunable thicknesses can achieve simultaneous high UV reflection and high SWIR transmission, and further refinement with reduced perturbation bounds (±0.5 nm) will improve target score convergence without destabilizing the solution.
current_route.design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics principle: alternating high-low refractive index layers form a Bragg reflector centered at the design wavelength. Quarter-wave optical thickness (n·d = λ₀/4) maximizes reflectance at the center wavelength. For dual-band operation, the reflection band is positioned at UV (center ~300 nm) while SWIR (800-1500 nm) falls outside the stopband for high transmission.
